name: FL-01
label: Safe R

model.rationale: The district's R+18 lean, incumbent Patronis's massive fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Republican win at about 95% all point the same way, with no polling or ratings suggesting movement. The forecast stays at a Safe R margin near -18.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Valimont within single digits, or a major outside-spending surge, would be the first sign of a real race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Florida's 1st District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of about R+18. Incumbent Jimmy Patronis, who won the seat in a special election, is running for a full term and holds a decisive financial advantage, having raised nearly $3.8 million with substantial outside support, while Democrat Gay Valimont has raised about $174,000.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals. Prediction markets give Valimont only about a 3% chance of winning. The seat is rated Safe Republican, with Patronis heavily favored to hold it.
